title: How emergence adds up
claim: For relations on bits, with logical emergence E: (1) joining two relations with all pairs free at one visible distinction gives E(R) + E(S) - log2(1 + bR bS), bR and bS the mean signs of the shared distinction, so visible parity chains hold one bit per knot; (2) forgetting coordinates never creates emergence from clauses of at most two literals, but the cyclic join of three copies of {000, 011, 101}, a least set of a pairwise energy, projects to parity (E = I = 1); (3) a ring of m >= 3 copies of a link with forgotten joints has E = -log2(1 - ((a+b)^m - (a-b)^m)/2), a and b the shares of identity and swap transfers, and a chain with visible ends has E = -log2(1 - z_m/4); both equal 1 at every length for parity and decay geometrically for every other link; (4) a law whose polymorphisms are all affine defines one-bit parity knots of every even size, while every other law's knots on N distinctions exclude at most N points and hold at most -log2(1 - N/2^N) bits; (5) on a simple graph with a knot link on every edge, hidden joints and visible spokes, E = -log2 Pr[the induced two-literal instance is satisfiable] <= b1 with equality exactly for parity, E is superadditive over edge-disjoint subgraphs (so a frustrating patch makes emergence grow with area), E = 0 for links with a common vacuum and for not-all-equal on bipartite graphs, and on a torus grid with an odd side not-all-equal recolours into uniformly random implications plus monotone seam clauses.
failure_conditions: A placement of two three-variable knots where the join formula fails or a pair of the join is constrained.
A projection of a majority-closed relation with positive emergence, or a gadget that is not a least set or does not project to parity.

A link whose ring disagrees with the formula, whose transfers are all permutations without being parity, a non-parity link whose chain does not decay, or a set of tables whose semigroup avoids the all-ones table outside the three families.
A conjunction- or disjunction-closed knot on three or four bits outside the stated shapes or above the bound.

A (link, graph) case with E above the cycle rank, a non-parity link reaching it, a vacuum link or a bipartite not-all-equal network with positive emergence, or a torus sample where the recoloured network disagrees.
foundation_claim_scope: How the emergence of systems of knots on bits adds up under joining, forgetting, chains, rings, laws and networks with hidden joints. No space, no metric, no physics.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies all 10,404 visible joins, forgetting on all 4,169 majority-closed relations on four bits and 271 random pairwise systems, the parity gadget by exact feasibility, rings and chains of all 204 placed three-variable links and all 742 four-variable knots, the semigroup step over all 127 sets of tables, the long-knot shapes on three and four bits, 1,836 (link, graph) network cases plus the Petersen graph, superadditivity examples and 600 torus recolouring samples; six controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive and sampled checks; the ring theorem, the full-product dichotomy, Post's lattice via BASE-THREE-20261021-001B-P001, the Galois connection and limited backtracking for two-literal instances are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found for projections of majority-closed relations and for the ring and chain decay (the ring theorem and the full-product dichotomy, restated in bits); candidate-local-delta for the cycle-rank bound with equality only for parity, superadditivity as emergence accounting, the long-knot dichotomy in laws, the torus recolouring, and the correction that non-parity links can hold many bits in large networks.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
